      "title": "Monotonicity conjecture for computing the Laplacian p-spectral radius",
      "statement": "Let $G$ be a graph, and for $p\\geq 1$ let $mu^{(p)}(G)$ denote its Laplacian $p$-spectral radius. Consider the computational problem of finding $mu^{(p)}(G)$ from the input graph $G$. **Computational monotonicity conjecture.** If $q>p\\geq 1$, then finding $mu^{(p)}(G)$ can be reduced to finding $mu^{(q)}(G)$ in polynomial time.\n\nThe conjecture is motivated by the fact that the cases $p=1$ and $p=\\infty$ have different computational behavior: the former is computable in linear time, whereas the latter is NP-complete. It proposes that increasing $p$ does not make the corresponding exact-value problem computationally easier.",

      "title": "Burns–Macedonska generalized Andrews–Curtis conjecture",
      "statement": "Let $G$ be a finitely generated group of rank $n$.   "342942": {

    "title": "Stahl's multichromatic-number conjecture for Kneser graphs",
    "literal_record": {
      "mathdb_id": 342942,
      "uuid": "2a0c5c49-7964-4de7-ab31-aedb25cd6986",
      "canonical_url": "https://mathdb.com/p/342942/stahl-s-multichromatic-number-conjecture-for-kneser-graphs",
      "title": "Stahl's multichromatic-number conjecture for Kneser graphs",
      "statement": "Let $K(m,n)$ be the Kneser graph whose vertices are the $n$-subsets of $\\{1,\\ldots,m\\}$, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding subsets are disjoint. For an integer $r$, let $\\chi_r(H)$ be the least integer $s$ such that $H$ admits a homomorphism to $K(s,r)$. **Stahl's conjecture.** If $k=an+b$, where $a\\geq 1$ and $0\\leq b\\leq n-1$, then for $m\\geq 2n$,\n\n$$\n\\chi_k(K(m,n))=\\chi_{an}(K(m,n))+\\chi_b(K(m,n))=(a+1)m-2(n-b).\n$$\n\nThis conjecture concerns the exact multichromatic numbers of Kneser graphs and is used in the paper to derive stronger lower bounds for chromatic numbers of exponential graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.",
      "statement_completeness": "full",
      "post_type": "conjecture",
      "status": "open",
      "tags": [
        "chromatic-number",
        "graph-theory",
        "kneser-graphs"

    "mathdb_id": 316166,
    "title": "Cameron–Erdős conjecture",
    "statement": "In combinatorics, the Cameron–Erdős conjecture (now a theorem) is the statement that the number of sum-free sets contained in $[N]=\\{1,\\ldots,N\\}$ is $O{\\big (}{2^{N/2}}{\\big)}.$ The sum of two odd numbers is even, so a set of odd numbers is always sum-free. There are $\\lceil N/2\\rceil$ odd numbers in [N ], and so $2^{N/2}$ subsets of odd numbers in [N ]. The Cameron–Erdős conjecture says that this counts a constant proportion of the sum-free sets. The conjecture was stated by Peter Cameron and Paul Erdős in 1988. It was proved by Ben Green and independently by Alexander Sapozhenko in 2003.",
